title: Cisco to add Anthropic Claude Mythos to harden AI agent security and operations
summary: Cisco integrates Anthropic Claude Mythos into its AI Defense red teaming tool
detailed: Cisco announced plans to integrate Anthropic's Claude Mythos into Cisco AI Defense to simulate real-world cyberattacks on AI agents.
Cisco added Tokenomics to Splunk Agent Observability to track AI agent token spending and ROI alongside Amazon Bedrock and CloudWatch data.
The company introduced Eval-G1, a small language model built to assess agent quality at up to 98% lower cost and 2.5x higher speed than commercial LLMs.
Red-team testing with Claude Mythos will roll out to select enterprise customers, while Tokenomics enters private preview in December.
sentences: Cisco will bring Anthropic's artificial intelligence (AI) model Claude Mythos to its security platform.

As more AI agents gain access to companies' internal systems and sensitive data, the company aims to counter AI-enabled cyberattacks while strengthening both the security and operating efficiency of those agents.
At its annual Cisco Live APJC event in Melbourne, Australia, Cisco said it will add Claude Mythos to Cisco AI Defense.
The core is to use Claude Mythos's advanced reasoning to run multi-step security tests that closely simulate real-world attacks on AI applications and agents and to uncover potential vulnerabilities.
The feature is limited to systems a company owns and has approved for testing, and every test goes through administrator authentication and an audit trail.
Scans of arbitrary internet infrastructure are restricted, and tests can be halted when needed.
Cisco also strengthened tools to manage AI agents' operating costs and performance together.
Tokenomics, which is being added to Splunk Agent Observability, analyzes token spending by AI agent alongside work quality using Amazon Bedrock and CloudWatch data.
With it, companies can track operating costs and gauge return on investment (ROI) for AI agents and coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
Quality evaluation for AI agents is also being added.
Eval-G1, a small language model (SLM) built on agent run logs and expert feedback, can assess agents and apply guardrails at up to 98% lower cost than commercial large language models (LLMs).
It also runs 2.5 times faster than LLMs.
An Evaluation Tuner, which lets companies adjust the evaluation model to their own quality standards, will be provided alongside it.
Cisco will also expand integration between Cisco IQ and the Splunk platform.

It will pipe Cisco IQ's vulnerability, product life-cycle, and configuration data into Splunk so security operations teams can analyze real-time threat intelligence alongside weaknesses in network infrastructure.
Through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and a ServiceNow connector, the system will link discovered vulnerabilities to related IT asset and incident records and automate response workflows.
Cisco IQ currently manages more than 16,000 customer organizations and about 20 million devices.
Jeetu Patel, Cisco's president and chief product officer (CPO), said, "Without security, governance, and observability, you cannot scale AI.

We are building a continuous trust framework that evaluates and controls AI agents' security and quality at machine speed."
Red-team testing with Claude Mythos will roll out soon to select enterprise customers.
Tokenomics will enter a private preview in December and launch on the AWS Marketplace in early 2027, while Eval-G1 and the Evaluation Tuner will be generally available starting in November.
